scale.description: Candidates and voters are positioned on each axis from -2 (fully pole_a) to +2 (fully pole_b); 0 = mixed/centrist on the axis. Voter weights per axis: 0 (don't care) to 2 (care a lot). Candidate scores must carry citations and a confidence level; low-confidence scores are excluded from alignment math.

axes.title: Taxes & revenue
axes.tension: Should Washington raise more revenue from high earners and wealth to fund public services, or hold the line and cut taxes?

pole_a.label: Limit & cut taxes
pole_a.description: Oppose new taxes (income, wealth, levy-cap lifts); prioritize reducing the tax burden

pole_b.label: Tax wealth to fund services
pole_b.description: Expand progressive revenue (millionaires tax, wealth tax, cap lifts) to fund public investment

axes.salience: The single most recurrent divider: LD43 senate (wealth-tax spread), LD32, LD36 senate (repeal vs architect), LD5, every levy measure, assessor race legislative agendas

axes.title: Spending & accountability
axes.tension: Is the bigger problem that government under-invests, or that it doesn't manage and audit what it already spends?

pole_a.label: Audit & restrain
pole_a.description: Oversight, audits, performance standards, and restraint before any new spending

pole_b.label: Invest & expand
pole_b.description: Expand programs and public investment as the primary lever for outcomes

axes.salience: Differentiates WITHIN parties: KCC D8 (accountability lane vs incumbent), LD32 senate (audit homelessness spending), LD33 P2, most R challengers; measures with ratchet/flexibility concerns

axes.title: Housing affordability
axes.tension: What fixes housing costs: unleashing market supply, or public investment and tenant protections?

pole_a.label: Market supply & deregulation
pole_a.description: Streamline permitting, cut red tape, let the market build; skepticism of rent regulation

pole_b.label: Public housing & tenant protections
pole_b.description: Social housing, rent stabilization, tenant right-to-counsel, public investment

axes.salience: Seattle D5 (three distinct positions), KCC D2 (social-housing levy timing), LD43 senate (rent-stabilization stringency), LD46, LD47

axes.title: Public safety & street disorder
axes.tension: Lead with enforcement and accountability, or with prevention, treatment, and non-police response?

pole_a.label: Enforcement & accountability
pole_a.description: Police staffing, prosecuting repeat offenders, mandatory treatment, clearing encampments

pole_b.label: Prevention & services
pole_b.description: Root causes, voluntary treatment, housing-first, community/non-police responders, diversion

axes.salience: Seattle D5 (sharpest), KCC D8 (three-strikes proposal), LD5 (police chief candidate), LD47, LD30; judicial races via prosecution-vs-defense formation and bail/diversion posture

axes.title: Climate & energy
axes.tension: Press forward on climate policy even when it raises costs, or prioritize energy affordability?

pole_a.label: Energy affordability first
pole_a.description: Repeal/pare back the Climate Commitment Act and gas taxes; expand all energy sources

pole_b.label: Climate action first
pole_b.description: Defend and extend carbon pricing, clean-energy transition, climate-resilient investment

axes.salience: LD36 senate (CCA architect vs repeal), LD33 P1 (eliminate CCA plank), CD9 (Basler's affordability critique), LD45 P1

axes.title: Record vs. renewal
axes.tension: Value a proven record and institutional effectiveness, or fresh perspectives and generational change?

pole_a.label: Proven record
pole_a.description: Incumbency, seniority, bills passed, institutional relationships that deliver

pole_b.label: New voices
pole_b.description: Outsider energy, generational change, lived experience over insider tenure

axes.salience: Appears in nearly every contested race; THE axis in LD37 P1, LD11 P1, CD1, CD7, and the appointment-pipeline argument in all four Supreme Court races

axes.title: Local control vs. regional consistency
axes.tension: Should decisions (zoning, schools, services) sit with the smallest local unit, or be set regionally/statewide for consistency?

pole_a.label: Local control
pole_a.description: City/parent/district control; skepticism of state mandates and regional consolidation

pole_b.label: Regional/state standards
pole_b.description: State housing mandates, regional authorities, county-level coordination

axes.salience: LD1 P2 (GMA rollback candidates), LD33 P2 (unfunded mandates), both fire-annexation measures, Covington park district

axes.title: Money & power in politics
axes.tension: How much does independence from institutional money and structural political reform matter?

pole_a.label: Work the system
pole_a.description: Coalition-building within existing party/donor structures gets results

pole_b.label: Reform the system
pole_b.description: Refuse PAC money; term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy

axes.salience: Central for Etzkorn (CD1), Gordon, Sawant/Chaudhry (CD9), Sabio-Howell (LD43), Brown (LD37), Leritz (LD5), Jacobson (KCC D8)

axes.title: Immigration & federal enforcement
axes.tension: Constrain federal immigration enforcement and protect immigrants, or prioritize enforcement and border security?

pole_a.label: Enforcement first
pole_a.description: Secure border, support ICE cooperation, enforcement of immigration law

pole_b.label: Protect immigrants
pole_b.description: Constrain ICE (masking bans, surveillance limits), sanctuary policies, legal pathways

axes.salience: CD7 (Jayapal's signature), CD9 (abolish-ICE spread), CD8 (R field), LD32 P2 (Siddiqi), LD46 senate, LD33 P1

axes.title: Healthcare system
axes.tension: Replace private insurance with a universal public system, or strengthen and fix the current system?

pole_a.label: Strengthen current system
pole_a.description: Protect ACA/Medicaid, cap drug prices, lower premiums within existing structures

pole_b.label: Single-payer transformation
pole_b.description: Medicare for All / universal public coverage as the goal

axes.salience: CD1 (three-way split), CD7, CD9 (mechanism/urgency differences), LD5 (Warmerdam single-payer), LD1 P2

axes.title: Gender, LGBTQ+ and reproductive policy
axes.tension: Should state law protect gender identity, LGBTQ+ rights and reproductive choice broadly (in school sports, medical care and anti-discrimination law), or set traditional sex-based and pro-life limits?

pole_a.label: Traditional values
pole_a.description: Sex-based eligibility for girls' and women's sports, limits on gender-affirming care for minors, pro-life positions, narrower anti-discrimination protections

pole_b.label: Progressive social policy
pole_b.description: Trans participation in sports by gender identity, reproductive and gender-affirming care as rights, broad anti-discrimination law

axes.salience: General ballot: I-638 (sex verification for girls' school sports) maps here. Primary evidence: LD47 P2 (DEI removal vs Members of Color Caucus chair), LD45 P1, LD41 P1, LD33 P1 (three-way spread), LD12 P2, LD46 senate. Curricula and parental-rights evidence now belongs to parental-rights.

axes.title: Parents and public schools
axes.tension: Should parents have broad notification, record access and opt-out rights over what schools teach and provide, or should schools and students have discretion?

pole_a.label: Parental notification and opt-out
pole_a.description: Parents notified of and able to review curricula, materials, records and school-provided health services; broad opt-out rights

pole_b.label: School and student discretion
pole_b.description: Educators set curricula under state standards; student privacy and confidentiality in some health and counseling matters; narrower opt-outs

axes.salience: General ballot: I-1 (parental rights in schools) maps here. Applies to state legislative contests, school-district and other school-adjacent measures, and statewide initiatives; never to judicial contests. Split from social so a voter can support one of I-1 and I-638 and oppose the other.

axes.title: AI & big tech
axes.tension: Regulate AI, data centers, and tech platforms aggressively, or keep Washington innovation-friendly?

pole_a.label: Innovation-friendly
pole_a.description: Light-touch regulation; treat tech/AI growth and its energy demand as opportunity

pole_b.label: Regulate aggressively
pole_b.description: AI guardrails, data-center limits/subsidy skepticism, platform accountability, data privacy

axes.salience: The novel axis this cycle: LD46 P1 (race's flashpoint, AI-industry money contested), LD32 P1 (Noble's platform), LD32 senate, LD45 P2, CD1 (halt data centers vs nationalize AI vs opportunity)

axes.title: Foreign policy & defense
axes.tension: Reduce military spending and conditions on aid (especially to Israel), or maintain defense commitments and alliances?

pole_a.label: Maintain commitments
pole_a.description: Strong defense budget, support allies including Israel, defense-industry partnership

pole_b.label: Reduce & recondition
pole_b.description: Arms embargo/aid conditions on Israel, audit/cut the Pentagon, end forever wars

axes.salience: CD9's clearest divider (HASC ranking member vs arms-embargo challengers), CD7 (War Powers), CD1

axes.title: Judicial philosophy
axes.tension: Should judges read law strictly as written, or pragmatically interpret it to protect rights as society changes?

pole_a.label: As written
pole_a.description: Strict construction, text and original meaning, judicial restraint, depoliticize the court

pole_b.label: Pragmatic & rights-protective
pole_b.description: State constitution as rights guarantor, law meeting the community where it is, openness to reform

axes.salience: SSC Pos 3 (clearest three-way philosophy spread), Pos 1 (rights-guarantor vs as-written), Pos 5 (posture toward Blake/bail), Pos 7 (Quinn/Blake critiques); Seattle Muni Court via bail/diversion posture

interview.authored_by: Hand-authored for this ballot from data/final/2026-11-03-general/rubric.json axes; each item maps agree -> a signed axis value. Statement directions are deliberately mixed so 'agree' alternates poles across the interview (acquiescence-bias guard).
interview.notes: value semantics: agree applies `value`, disagree applies `-value`, skip applies nothing. weight from care pulse: not-much=0.5, default=1, a-lot=2. Scenarios apply every effect listed for the chosen option. General-election changes (issue #4, 2026-10-08): card-social reworded to the narrowed social axis and flipped to value 2; card-parental-rights added with value -2 so agree keeps alternating poles (healthcare -2, social +2, parental-rights -2, tech +2, defense -2).

Before asking taxpayers for anything new, government should first prove it spends what it already has well.
The county finds a budget surplus. Where should it go first?

options.label: Hiring more police officers
options.detail: Faster response times and more patrols

items.text: The fastest fix for housing costs is cutting permits and regulations so builders can build more.
Climate policies like carbon pricing are worth it, even when they raise gas and energy prices.
I'd rather have an experienced insider who knows how to get things done than a newcomer with fresh ideas.
Two housing bills reach the governor's desk, but only one gets funded. Which one?

options.label: Cut red tape for builders
options.detail: Streamlined permits, relaxed zoning — let supply catch up

options.label: Public housing & renter protections
options.detail: Social housing dollars, rent stabilization, right to counsel

items.text: Zoning and school decisions belong with each city and community — not with the state.
I trust a candidate more when they refuse PAC and corporate money.
State and local government should limit how much they cooperate with federal immigration enforcement.
Healthcare works better when we improve the system we have, rather than replacing private insurance with one public plan.
Olympia faces a budget shortfall. What should legislators reach for first?

options.label: Cut programs & find efficiencies
options.detail: Tighten belts before touching anyone's taxes

options.label: New taxes on the wealthiest
options.detail: Protect services by asking more from those with the most

items.text: State law should protect transgender people's rights, including playing on school sports teams that match their gender identity.
Parents should be able to see their child's school records and opt their child out of lessons or school services they object to.
AI companies and data centers need much stricter rules here, even if that slows the local tech economy.
The U.S. should keep supporting allies like Israel with military aid, without adding new conditions.
Judges should stick to the exact text of the law as written — even when a strict reading produces harsh results.

contests.race_blurb: Incumbent Suzan DelBene (D), in office since 2012 and chair of House Democrats' campaign committee, faces Republican Mary Silva, an Everett audiologist making her first run beyond party precinct posts. DelBene led the primary with 53% to Silva's 26%.

candidates.name: Suzan DelBene
candidates.summary: U.S. Representative since 2012 on the Ways and Means Committee and 2026 chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee; former Microsoft executive and state Revenue director.
highlights: Campaigns on lowering costs, a permanent expanded Child Tax Credit and having "the wealthy pay their fair share" [S1]
Introduced the CHEATERS Act in July 2026 to restore $83 billion in IRS funding aimed at high-income tax evasion [S6]
Wants to roll back Medicaid cuts, lower premiums and "rein in out-of-control ICE agents" [S1]
Supports reproductive rights and opposes a nationwide abortion ban; voted against H.R. 28 on girls' sports in 2025 [S1][S15]
Said in July that "Americans should not be subsidizing" the Netanyahu government's conduct, while voting against the Massie amendment that would have cut aid [S7][S9]

taxes.basis: Says the wealthy must pay their fair share and sponsored the CHEATERS Act on high-income tax enforcement, while also seeking tax cuts for working families rather than new progressive taxes.

spending.basis: Platform expands programs (permanent monthly Child Tax Credit, reversing Medicaid and food-assistance cuts, two million affordable homes) without an audit-first theme.

climate.basis: Criticizes cuts to green-energy investment, sponsored the carbon-based Clean Competition Act, and voted against rolling back EPA approvals of California emission rules.

experience.basis: Fourteen years in the House on Ways and Means with an enacted bill, plus prior service as state Revenue director.

reform.basis: Chairs the DCCC, her party's national House campaign operation, and raised about $1.48 million of $3.55 million from political committees.

immigration.basis: Calls for immigration reform and reining in "out-of-control ICE agents" in her pamphlet; no sponsored immigration bills recorded in the dossier.

healthcare.basis: Health agenda works within the current system: lower premiums, restore Medicaid, strengthen Medicare, and oversight of Medicare's AI claims-review program; no single-payer position.

social.basis: States strong support for reproductive rights and opposition to a national abortion ban, and voted against H.R. 28 restricting girls' sports by sex.

tech.basis: Repeated sponsor of the Email Privacy Act and other digital-privacy bills; seeking disclosure on AI-driven Medicare claim reviews.

defense.basis: Says the U.S. should not subsidize the Netanyahu government's conduct and voted against the anti-boycott bill and FY2027 NDAA, but voted against the Massie amendment cutting aid.

tech.basis: Would dismantle warrantless surveillance, require warrants for location and video data, and impose cybersecurity requirements on federal contractors.

defense.basis: Calls for a comprehensive Pentagon audit and curbs on military-contractor payouts; her site hosts a video titled "How Does Netanyahu Get Away With War Crimes?"

candidates.name: Pramila Jayapal
candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative since 2017 and former state senator; Chair Emerita of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and ranking member of the House Immigration Subcommittee.
highlights: Leads the Medicare for All Act and backs an ultra-millionaire wealth tax [S1]
Authored the Iran War Powers resolution that passed the House 214-208 in July 2026; voted against the FY2027 NDAA [S5][S6]
Released a National AI Charter Act framework in October 2026 requiring AI companies to hold a federal charter [S8]
Co-chairs the Trans Equality Task Force; endorsed by Planned Parenthood, the State Labor Council and Fuse Washington [S1][S11]
Raised about $2.5 million through the pre-primary report [S3]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet backs an ultra-millionaire wealth tax; sponsored the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act of 2026 (H.R. 8085).

spending.basis: Leads bills to expand federal programs: Medicare for All, tuition-free college, housing as a human right.

safety.basis: Sponsored the Housing not Handcuffs Act and a moratorium on government facial-recognition use, pointing toward non-enforcement responses.

climate.basis: Pamphlet says she works to fight climate change and is Sierra Club-endorsed; no specific 2026 climate bill recorded.

experience.basis: Ten years in the House with subcommittee ranking-member and caucus leadership roles.

reform.basis: Says she never takes corporate PAC money and leads a congressional stock-trading ban and Supreme Court reform; FEC shows $280,500 from other political committees, so not a full pole_b case.

immigration.basis: Campaigns against 'lawless ICE and CBP actions,' sponsored the ICE Out of Our Faces and Dignity for Detained Immigrants Acts, and opposes rescissions targeting immigration services.

healthcare.basis: Leads the Medicare for All Act, framing universal healthcare as a right.

social.basis: Co-chairs the Trans Equality Task Force, sponsored a Transgender Bill of Rights resolution, and campaigns on protecting abortion rights.

tech.basis: National AI Charter Act framework (federal charters, pre-release testing, kill switch, strict liability) and a biometric-surveillance moratorium.

defense.basis: Voted against the FY2027 NDAA, for the Massie amendment to cut Israel military aid, and authored the Iran War Powers resolution.

candidates.name: Kim Schrier
candidates.summary: U.S. Representative since 2019 and former Issaquah pediatrician on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, seeking a fifth term.
highlights: Cites bills capping insulin costs and letting Medicare negotiate drug prices; wants Medicaid cuts and ACA premium credits reversed [S1][S3]
Introduced a bill to suspend the federal gas tax through year's end; her hydropower licensing bill became law in September 2026 [S1][S9]
Pro-choice; says she twice voted for the Women's Health Protection Act and voted against H.R. 28 on girls' sports [S4][S17]
Supports border security plus a path to citizenship and codifying DACA [S5]
Says she secured over $60 million in district projects, including body cameras and a rapid DNA system for King County law enforcement [S1]

taxes.basis: Proposes suspending the federal gas tax while criticizing Republican tax cuts for billionaires; no proposal for new progressive taxes.

spending.basis: Highlights $60 million in district projects and wants restored Medicaid and ACA credits plus more community health centers and school-based clinics.

safety.basis: Pledges to fight any effort to defund police and funded body cameras and a rapid DNA system for King County law enforcement, while also backing mental-health professionals alongside police.

climate.basis: Says climate change requires immediate action and voted against rolling back EPA approvals of California emission rules; also proposes a gas-tax suspension and backs hydropower and fusion.

experience.basis: Four terms in the House on Energy and Commerce, with a bill signed into law in 2026.

immigration.basis: Backs a path to citizenship and codifying DACA and says the administration is "terrorizing immigrant communities," while also calling for a secure border.

healthcare.basis: Health record and platform work within the existing system: insulin caps, Medicare drug negotiation, restoring Medicaid and ACA credits, community health centers; no single-payer position.

social.basis: Pro-choice and says she twice voted to codify Roe; voted against H.R. 28 restricting girls' sports by sex.

tech.basis: Says she led a bill to protect children's data from Big Tech and that "we need regulations to protect people and their data."

defense.basis: Voted for H.R. 4795 barring college boycotts of Israel (most Democrats opposed) and against the Massie amendment to cut aid; voted against the FY2027 NDAA.

candidates.name: Spencer Meline
candidates.summary: Leavenworth restaurant owner and first-time candidate endorsed by the state, King County and Snohomish County Republican parties.
highlights: Running on housing costs and small business; proposes first-time homebuyer tax relief, limits on institutional buyers of starter homes and a portable-mortgage pilot [S4][S6]
Supports congressional term limits, single-subject bills and a ban on members trading individual stocks [S4]
Calls for enforceable restraints on deficit growth and cuts to waste and unnecessary spending [S4]
Backs "all-of-the-above" energy including hydropower, nuclear, renewables, natural gas and domestic oil [S4]
Says "We shouldn't allow illegal entry at all" but is open to bipartisan reform of legal immigration [S5]

taxes.basis: Proposes tax incentives for small businesses, first-time homebuyer tax relief, capital-gains changes and tax-deductible premiums; no new taxes proposed.

spending.basis: Platform calls for enforceable restraints on deficit growth, cutting waste and unnecessary spending, and plain-English spending transparency.

climate.basis: All-of-the-above energy including natural gas and domestic oil to keep costs manageable, alongside hydropower, solar and fusion; no climate-policy commitments.

experience.basis: Never held office; runs as "not a politician" on small-business experience.

reform.basis: Platform backs congressional term limits, single-subject bills and a ban on individual stock trading by members; also runs with state and county party endorsements.

immigration.basis: Prioritizes border security and says illegal entry should not be allowed at all, while saying he is open to bipartisan reform of legal pathways.

tech.basis: Pairs "Government shouldn't try to stop innovation" and AI leadership goals with strong federal privacy law, antitrust enforcement against dominant tech firms and AI accountability.

contests.office_does: A U.S. Representative writes and votes on federal legislation, controls federal spending through appropriations, oversees the executive branch, and provides constituent services for the district.
contests.race_blurb: Incumbent Adam Smith (D), in the House since 1997 and top Democrat on Armed Services, faces Republican Doug Basler for the sixth time. Smith took 47% and Basler 22% in a primary where two left-flank challengers split much of the remainder.

candidates.name: Adam Smith
candidates.summary: Incumbent U.S. Representative since 1997, former state senator and Seattle prosecutor; ranking member and past chair of the House Armed Services Committee.
highlights: Voted against the FY2027 NDAA in July 2026, citing its $1.6 trillion price tag and anti-LGBTQ+ floor amendments [S6][S13]
Voted to block $3.3 billion in Israel military aid while saying he still supports Israel [S7][S14]
Introduced a resolution to tax capital gains the same as wages [S8]
Supports a path to single-payer healthcare and lists protecting abortion rights as a priority [S1][S3]
Endorsed by the Seattle Times, King County Democrats, Gov. Ferguson and the State Labor Council [S4]

taxes.basis: Introduced a resolution to tax capital gains like wages, saying the ultra-wealthy pay too little; no wealth tax.

spending.basis: Platform invests in housing, job training and workforce programs and opposes domestic cuts, while citing the deficit against the defense budget increase.

safety.basis: Bills on the 988 crisis line and behavioral-health crisis care centers point toward services responses.

climate.basis: Lists protecting Puget Sound and voted against overturning EPA approval of California's at-berth emission standards.

experience.basis: In Congress since 1997, Armed Services ranking member and past chair, with enacted bills.

reform.basis: Accepts PAC money ($563,000 from other committees this cycle) and runs on broad party and union endorsements; no structural-reform planks recorded.

immigration.basis: Co-introduced bills to help immigrants enter the health-care workforce.

healthcare.basis: Repeatedly says the system should be restructured toward 'a path to a single-payer plan like Medicare for All.'

social.basis: Protecting abortion rights is a campaign priority; opposes the transgender military ban and objected to anti-LGBTQ+ NDAA amendments; endorsed by HRC PAC and Planned Parenthood.

defense.basis: Mixed: voted against the FY2027 NDAA on cost and to block $3.3B in Israel aid, and backed the Iran War Powers resolution, while stating continued support for Israel and a strong defense.

contests.race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Davina Duerr, chair of the House Local Government Committee, faces first-time Republican candidate Maggie Wang; Duerr took about three quarters of the primary vote. The race contrasts Duerr's vote for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million with Wang's pledge to stop tax increases and audit state spending.

candidates.name: Davina Duerr
candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2019 and chair of the House Local Government Committee, an architect and former Bothell deputy mayor whose record centers housing supply, permitting and growth management.
highlights: Lists seven bills that became law last term, including cheaper affordable-housing construction, faster housing permits and a growth-management loophole fix [S1]
Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal, and co-signed a session report calling it a historic step [S3][S6]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list [S4]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million and co-signed a session report praising it as fixing an upside-down tax code.

housing.basis: Housing record centers supply-side measures: streamlining permits, cutting permitting delays (HB 2418) and lowering construction costs, rather than tenant protections.

local-control.basis: Chairs Local Government and passed state-level rules on growth management and local permitting timelines, setting standards for cities.

climate.basis: Lists a bill phasing out super-pollutant refrigerants and is endorsed by Washington Conservation Action; no stated position on carbon pricing.

experience.basis: In office since 2019, committee chair, seven bills enacted last term; opponent has never held office.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no statement of her own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which modified and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.name: Shelley Kloba
candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2017 and Vice-Chair of the House Technology, Economic Development, and Veterans Committee, focused on data privacy, AI guardrails and tax-code changes.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and calls it the start of correcting an upside-down tax code [S2][S5]
Prime sponsor of the People's Privacy Act (HB 1671) and a data-broker registry bill [S8]

taxes.basis: Voted for the Millionaires Tax and defends it and the capital gains tax as correcting an upside-down tax code, pledging further 'fair tax' bills.

spending.basis: Platform emphasizes fully funding K-12, behavioral-health access and renewable-energy investment rather than audits or restraint.

safety.basis: Highlights crisis-responder teams and crisis treatment centers law enforcement can use instead of jail or the ER.

climate.basis: Supports reducing dependence on fossil fuels, renewable-energy investment and green jobs in pamphlet and website; endorsed by Sierra Club.

experience.basis: Nine years in the House, committee vice-chair, bills enacted; opponent has never held office beyond PCO.

healthcare.basis: Says health care is 'a right, not a privilege', should never be tied to employment, and calls for 'getting rid of the middleman'; no explicit single-payer proposal.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Washington Stonewall Democrats; no statement of her own beyond protecting civil rights.

parental-rights.basis: Original sponsor of and yes vote on ESHB 1296, which modified and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list.

tech.basis: Record centers data-privacy and AI regulation: People's Privacy Act, data-broker registry bill, AI consumer-harm work; says AI should not exploit people for profit.

candidates.name: Jesse Salomon
candidates.summary: Two-term incumbent state senator and Local Government Committee chair who supports the millionaires tax but opposes extending it, and pledges to audit spending.
highlights: Pulled SB 6346 (millionaires tax) from Senate Rules and voted for it, but calls a $250,000 threshold "incredibly out of touch" [S6][S7]

taxes.basis: Voted for and backs the $1 million income tax, but rejects extending it and says more revenue should have gone to tax relief rather than the operating budget.

spending.basis: Pamphlet says government must be more responsible with tax dollars and pledges to audit spending.

housing.basis: Wrote permitting and supply bills and also voted for rent stabilization; a genuine mix of both poles.

safety.basis: Describes a balanced enforcement-and-treatment approach, criticizing the Blake overcorrection while backing treatment, housing and officer decertification.

climate.basis: Says he sponsored the Climate Commitment Act and supported a fracking ban and clean-energy investment.

experience.basis: Incumbent senator since 2019 and committee chair with bills passed each session.

immigration.basis: Cites banning ICE face masks and co-sponsoring judicial-warrant and audit-notice protections.

healthcare.basis: Health priorities are price accountability and oversight within the existing system; no universal-coverage proposal.

social.basis: Says he is 100% pro-choice, sponsored SB 5400 shielding providers, and supports a constitutional right to reproductive care.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

tech.basis: Cites leading the fight to block AI-powered rent-setting schemes.

candidates.name: Ted Cooke
candidates.summary: Republican software tester and team lead from Covington, a precinct committee officer since 2009 and former King County GOP 2nd Vice Chair. He lost this seat to Stearns in 2024.
highlights: Would freeze new taxes, eliminate taxes on income, property and fuel, and audit every state office [S1]
Would 'restore full parental rights in education' and post school curricula online for parental review [S1][S4]
Pledges to 'uphold the biological definition of gender' [S1]
Would end cap-and-trade and lower or eliminate the gas tax [S4]
Prefers 'starter homes with yards over high-density apartments forced on us by Olympia' [S1]

taxes.basis: Would freeze all new taxes and eliminate income, property and fuel taxes, and wants the capital gains tax eliminated.

spending.basis: Would audit every state office and program, cut waste, and stop increases in government spending.

housing.basis: Would ease the Growth Management Act, streamline permitting and cut taxes to spur building, while opposing state-driven high-density apartments.

safety.basis: Public safety first; would let police act on reasonable suspicion rather than probable cause and keep 'anti-police' members off use-of-force review boards.

climate.basis: Would end cap-and-trade (the Climate Commitment Act's mechanism) and eliminate fuel taxes to cut energy costs.

local-control.basis: Opposes 'high-density apartments forced on us by Olympia', would ease the Growth Management Act, and would end legislative commissions.

social.basis: Pledges to 'uphold the biological definition of gender'; a single repeated pamphlet line, with no other gender or reproductive policy detail.

parental-rights.basis: Would 'restore full parental rights in education', give parents 'oversight of children and education', and post all curricula online for parental review.

experience.basis: Has never held public office; party officer and 2024 challenger.

taxes.basis: Reported to support progressive revenue restructuring and proposed a new tax on AI data centers; no broader tax platform on her site.

spending.basis: Platform proposes new or expanded programs (fully funded 24/7 CARE Department, free transit for all students, 1,000 affordable units) without a restraint or audit plank.

housing.basis: Affordable-housing unit target built through public land and nonprofit partnerships, plus rent stabilization, just-cause eviction and tenant right to counsel.

safety.basis: Leads with CARE Department, community court and violence intervention and opposes SOAP and camera expansion, while also supporting a 1,200-officer target and a North Seattle precinct.

climate.basis: Pledges to 'move us toward meeting our climate goals' and is described as a climate advocate who ties density and transit to climate goals.

experience.basis: Has not held elected office; brings advocacy and political-organizing experience and a prior run for this seat.

reform.basis: Works professionally on voting reform at FairVote Washington and lists implementing ranked-choice voting in 2027 as a priority.

candidates.name: Gabe Rothstein

judicial.basis: Calls the court "the people's court" and centers treatment, second chances and dignity; evidence unchanged since the primary.

safety.basis: Explicit position against wealth-based detention, treatment over punishment, drug-court and recovery-board service and a 20-year defense formation; re-verified on his site, unchanged since the primary.

experience.basis: Mixed: two decades of practice and a KCBA Well Qualified rating, but pro tem service only since 2024.

candidates.name: Suzan DelBene
candidates.summary: U.S. Representative since 2012 on the Ways and Means Committee and 2026 chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee; former Microsoft executive and state Revenue director.
highlights: Campaigns on lowering costs, a permanent expanded Child Tax Credit and having "the wealthy pay their fair share" [S1]
Introduced the CHEATERS Act in July 2026 to restore $83 billion in IRS funding aimed at high-income tax evasion [S6]
Wants to roll back Medicaid cuts, lower premiums and "rein in out-of-control ICE agents" [S1]
Supports reproductive rights and opposes a nationwide abortion ban; voted against H.R. 28 on girls' sports in 2025 [S1][S15]
Said in July that "Americans should not be subsidizing" the Netanyahu government's conduct, while voting against the Massie amendment that would have cut aid [S7][S9]

taxes.basis: Says the wealthy must pay their fair share and sponsored the CHEATERS Act on high-income tax enforcement, while also seeking tax cuts for working families rather than new progressive taxes.

spending.basis: Platform expands programs (permanent monthly Child Tax Credit, reversing Medicaid and food-assistance cuts, two million affordable homes) without an audit-first theme.

climate.basis: Criticizes cuts to green-energy investment, sponsored the carbon-based Clean Competition Act, and voted against rolling back EPA approvals of California emission rules.

experience.basis: Fourteen years in the House on Ways and Means with an enacted bill, plus prior service as state Revenue director.

reform.basis: Chairs the DCCC, her party's national House campaign operation, and raised about $1.48 million of $3.55 million from political committees.

immigration.basis: Calls for immigration reform and reining in "out-of-control ICE agents" in her pamphlet; no sponsored immigration bills recorded in the dossier.

healthcare.basis: Health agenda works within the current system: lower premiums, restore Medicaid, strengthen Medicare, and oversight of Medicare's AI claims-review program; no single-payer position.

social.basis: States strong support for reproductive rights and opposition to a national abortion ban, and voted against H.R. 28 restricting girls' sports by sex.

tech.basis: Repeated sponsor of the Email Privacy Act and other digital-privacy bills; seeking disclosure on AI-driven Medicare claim reviews.

defense.basis: Says the U.S. should not subsidize the Netanyahu government's conduct and voted against the anti-boycott bill and FY2027 NDAA, but voted against the Massie amendment cutting aid.

candidates.name: Rick Larsen
candidates.summary: Thirteen-term incumbent and lead Democrat on the House Transportation & Infrastructure Committee, running on lowering costs, health care access, ICE accountability, abortion rights and infrastructure funding.
highlights: Will not vote for full-year DHS and ICE funding without oversight; voted against the Laken Riley Act [S2][S7]
Calls health care a right and backs universal coverage, with a record of ACA and Medicare cost measures [S2]
Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act and calls climate mitigation a top priority [S2][S8]
Supports the Women's Health Protection Act and cites a 100% voting record on choice [S2]
Voted for the 2024 Israel and Ukraine security supplementals [S9][S10]

taxes.basis: Supports scrapping the cap on income subject to Social Security taxes and voted against the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act; no broader wealth-tax position stated.

spending.basis: Backs expanded child care, a $17 minimum wage, Medicare hearing benefits and infrastructure investment; voted for the Inflation Reduction Act.

safety.basis: On fentanyl pairs 'addiction is a disease' and prevention/recovery funding with strengthening law enforcement against traffickers.

climate.basis: Says mitigating climate change must be a top priority, supports clean energy, and voted for the Inflation Reduction Act.

experience.basis: Thirteenth-term incumbent and lead Democrat on Transportation & Infrastructure, facing a first-time candidate.

immigration.basis: Conditions DHS/ICE funding on oversight, wants ICE body cameras and visible ID, supports ending family detention and private detention, and voted against the Laken Riley Act.

healthcare.basis: States universal coverage as a goal but his record and proposals work through ACA and Medicare; no single-payer proposal.

social.basis: Supports suspending the filibuster to pass the Women's Health Protection Act, cites a 100% pro-choice record, endorsed by Planned Parenthood Action Fund and Stonewall Democrats.

tech.basis: Calls for 'strong guardrails' on data centers so their power and water costs are not passed to ratepayers.

defense.basis: Voted for the 2024 Israel and Ukraine security supplementals while opposing 'reckless foreign wars.'

reform.basis: S2: has voted for legislation to 'end partisan gerrymandering, require disclosure of dark money, expand opportunities to vote' (dark-money disclosure is a named pole-B item).

candidates.name: Kim Schrier
candidates.summary: U.S. Representative since 2019 and former Issaquah pediatrician on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, seeking a fifth term.
highlights: Cites bills capping insulin costs and letting Medicare negotiate drug prices; wants Medicaid cuts and ACA premium credits reversed [S1][S3]
Introduced a bill to suspend the federal gas tax through year's end; her hydropower licensing bill became law in September 2026 [S1][S9]
Pro-choice; says she twice voted for the Women's Health Protection Act and voted against H.R. 28 on girls' sports [S4][S17]
Supports border security plus a path to citizenship and codifying DACA [S5]
Says she secured over $60 million in district projects, including body cameras and a rapid DNA system for King County law enforcement [S1]

taxes.basis: Proposes suspending the federal gas tax while criticizing Republican tax cuts for billionaires; no proposal for new progressive taxes.

spending.basis: Highlights $60 million in district projects and wants restored Medicaid and ACA credits plus more community health centers and school-based clinics.

safety.basis: Pledges to fight any effort to defund police and funded body cameras and a rapid DNA system for King County law enforcement, while also backing mental-health professionals alongside police.

climate.basis: Says climate change requires immediate action and voted against rolling back EPA approvals of California emission rules; also proposes a gas-tax suspension and backs hydropower and fusion.

experience.basis: Four terms in the House on Energy and Commerce, with a bill signed into law in 2026.

immigration.basis: Backs a path to citizenship and codifying DACA and says the administration is "terrorizing immigrant communities," while also calling for a secure border.

healthcare.basis: Health record and platform work within the existing system: insulin caps, Medicare drug negotiation, restoring Medicaid and ACA credits, community health centers; no single-payer position.

social.basis: Pro-choice and says she twice voted to codify Roe; voted against H.R. 28 restricting girls' sports by sex.

tech.basis: Says she led a bill to protect children's data from Big Tech and that "we need regulations to protect people and their data."

local-control.basis: Chairs Local Government and passed state-level rules on growth management and local permitting timelines, setting standards for cities.

climate.basis: Lists a bill phasing out super-pollutant refrigerants and is endorsed by Washington Conservation Action; no stated position on carbon pricing.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which modified and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

contests.office_does: The U.S. Representative for Washington's 5th District votes on federal law, taxes, spending and oversight for 12 Eastern Washington counties, including Spokane.
contests.race_blurb: A 2024 rematch: first-term Republican Michael Baumgartner, who led the August primary with 48%, faces Democrat Carmela Conroy, a former diplomat and deputy prosecutor who took 20.8%. They split on the 2025 tax-and-spending law, tariffs, immigration enforcement, the Iran war and Israel aid, and gender-affirming care for minors.

candidates.name: Michael Baumgartner
candidates.summary: First-term Republican congressman, former Spokane County Treasurer and state senator, running on tax cuts, border security and defense.
highlights: Voted for the 2025 tax and spending law (H.R. 1) on passage and final concurrence [S10]
Voted for the SAVE Act and the Laken Riley Act [S11]
Backs higher military spending and cuts to social services, citing the national debt [S16]
Supports a federal ban on gender-affirming care for minors [S14]
Sponsored a bill to bar members of Congress from trading individual stocks [S1]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2025 H.R. 1 tax cuts, campaigns on having reduced taxes, and calls a state income tax 'terrible'.

spending.basis: Calls for curbing 'reckless government spending' and cutting social services, but backs higher defense spending, so restraint is selective.

immigration.basis: Strongly supports border security and enforcement, voted for the Laken Riley Act, and calls the crackdown 'largely successful' while criticizing some ICE operations.

social.basis: Supports and says he voted for a federal ban on gender-affirming care for minors; leaves abortion law to the states.

defense.basis: Supports continuing the Iran conflict 'as long as it takes', U.S. aid to Israel, and a larger defense budget.

climate.basis: Applauded withdrawal from the Columbia Basin agreement, defends the Snake River dams, and dismisses 'environmental fads'.

tech.basis: Frames AI as a race with China and offers federal incentives for data centers, with a requirement that they pay for their power and water costs.

reform.basis: Sponsored legislation banning individual stock trading by members of Congress.

experience.basis: Incumbent congressman with prior service as county treasurer and state senator.

healthcare.basis: Official site backs a 'patient-centered' system where Americans are not 'forced to follow bureaucratic directives', working within the existing structure (rural hospital fund) [S5]; he supports the H.R. 1 Medicaid eligibility restrictions as cost-cutting [S16]. Clearly not single-payer; -1 rather than -2 because pole_a's 'protect ACA/Medicaid' does not describe him.

sources.ref: VoteWA voters' guide, Spokane County, GENERAL 2026, race 186951 (candidate statement)

reform.basis: Supports a congressional stock-trading ban and accountability for people named in the Epstein files.

spending.basis: Campaign pledges to cut waste and protect taxpayer dollars; voted against the 2025-27 state operating budget.

housing.basis: Would cut red tape, streamline county permitting and push for development-friendly state rules on housing.

safety.basis: Platform says she will back law enforcement and keep criminals off the streets; also supports replacing the jail with a facility that includes treatment.

experience.basis: Two-term state representative and ranking committee member who says eight of her bills became law.

candidates.name: Natasha Hill
candidates.summary: One-term Democratic incumbent, Vice Chair of the House Housing Committee and civil litigation attorney from Hillyard, whose record includes votes for the 2026 millionaires tax and the 2025 rent-increase limits.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal, and says she "led on" it [S1][S3]
Voted for the 2025 limits on rent and fee increases (EHB 1217) and has called for rent stabilization [S5][S9]
Voted for ESHB 1296 and is listed as opposing I-001 and I-638 [S4][S10]

taxes.basis: Voted for ESSB 6346; independently says she led on the millionaire tax, platform calls for the wealthy to pay an equitable share, and backed keeping the capital gains tax.

spending.basis: Co-wrote an op-ed urging rejection of child-care and early-learning cuts; platform supports investment in treatment, housing and job training.

housing.basis: Voted for EHB 1217 rent-increase limits and called for statewide rent stabilization, while also backing supply measures such as condominium reform and land banks.

safety.basis: Says incarceration without care is not effective and supports investment in mental health, addiction treatment, housing and job training.

climate.basis: Platform supports a just transition away from fossil fuels and clean-energy investment; no specific carbon-pricing record in the dossier.

experience.basis: Incumbent since 2025 with two sessions and a committee vice chair post; shorter tenure than a long-serving legislator, against a never-elected opponent.

immigration.basis: Says she supported critical protections for immigrants; co-wrote an op-ed criticizing federal prosecution of ICE-facility protesters.

social.basis: Platform pledges to champion safe access to abortion; publicly listed as opposing I-638.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights law, and is listed as opposing I-001, which would restore it.

sources.ref: VoteWA voters' guide, Spokane County, GENERAL 2026, race 186961 (candidate statement)

candidates.name: Natalie Poulson
candidates.summary: Republican special-education teacher and former Spokane Public Schools employee, running again after losing to Ormsby in 2022, on lower taxes, spending audits, enforcement-first public safety and parental rights.
highlights: Will "stand against any form of state income tax" and wants to repeal or lower the B&O tax [S2][S6]

taxes.basis: Opposes any state income tax and new broad-based taxes and would repeal or lower the B&O tax, in repeated statements.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for independent audits, cutting bureaucracy and not renewing programs without results.

housing.basis: "Supply-side solutions, not more spending or mandates": cut permitting delays, fees and state construction mandates, favor market-rate housing.

safety.basis: "Enforcement first," ending catch-and-release, custody or mandatory programs for repeat offenders, involuntary treatment and treatment-first over housing-first.

climate.basis: Opposes natural-gas restrictions in new construction on cost grounds; no broader climate-policy statement.

experience.basis: Never held public office beyond precinct committee officer; runs as a non-politician seeking change after 30 years of the same representation.

local-control.basis: Advocates local control of housing decisions and wants to stop Olympia from piling on construction rules.

immigration.basis: Opposes state suits against federal immigration enforcement and sanctuary incentives; supports cooperation on serious criminals.

social.basis: Pro-life and supports parental consent and limits on irreversible gender-affirming procedures for minors, while respecting current abortion law and adult choice.

parental-rights.basis: Names parental rights as a platform plank (families, not government, make decisions for children) without specific notification or opt-out proposals.

tech.basis: Opposes broad AI regulation as harmful to innovation but would roll back data-center tax exemptions.

tech.basis: Supports impact assessments and audits for high-risk AI, a ban on algorithmic discrimination, data protection and tighter data-center exemptions.

candidates.name: Rob Chase

experience.basis: Two House terms and eight years as county treasurer, facing a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Opposes abortion except for ectopic pregnancy and supported the initiative barring athletes assigned male at birth from girls' sports; cites a perfect Family Policy Institute score.

parental-rights.basis: Supported the I-1 parental-rights initiative, voted against ESHB 1296 and for faster parent access to special-education evaluations.

tech.basis: Supports building AI data centers unless they significantly affect nearby residents.

candidates.name: Jonathan Bingle
candidates.summary: Republican former Spokane City Councilmember (2022-2025), small-business owner and pastor, running on lower taxes, public safety, treatment-first homelessness policy and parental rights.

housing.basis: Blames regulation and impact fees for costs and backs market-led supply; council votes to drop parking mandates and downtown height limits.

safety.basis: Council record criminalizing open drug use and park-hours violations; platform of tougher penalties and treatment-first homelessness policy.

climate.basis: Would repeal or roll back the Climate Commitment Act and opposes carbon policies that raise fuel costs.

social.basis: Council amendment and platform to ban gender-affirming treatment for minors and restrict trans participation in girls' sports; supports a 13-week abortion limit.

parental-rights.basis: Platform calls for full curriculum transparency, parental notification in all school matters and school choice.

experience.basis: One Spokane City Council term (2022-2025); no legislative tenure; opponent is a first-time candidate.
